# Change-cost live runs, 2026-11-18

What this is: five small tasks (`eval/tasks/cc-*`) that each target a change-cost failure from the follow-up assignment, run
against the live gateway model with the **branch build** (`v1/invariants-impl`) and the **base build** (`65c76b28`), same
config (`eval/configs/pilot-nexus.json`: model `engineering/lead`, gateway 10.0.8.5, 65536 context), one run at a time under
the `GATEWAY` claim. Raw per-run rows: `run*-*.results.jsonl`; run manifests: `run*-*.manifest.json`. These are the real-Nexus
runs. The CERI scenarios A to H in `cli/test/fixtures/ceri/` stay mechanism-level and are reported separately.

| Task (scenario) | What the hidden check measures | Run 1 base | Run 1 branch | Run 2 base | Run 2 branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cc-minimal-fix (A/B/E) | bug fixed; no new file, no other file changed | 3/5 | 4/5 | 5/10 | 6/10 |
| cc-refactor-edge (G) | refactor keeps behaviour on rounding edge cases; duplication removed | 5/5 | 5/5 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| cc-keep-rationale (F) | simplifying keeps the behaviour its comment explains (empty PORT falls back) | 1/5 | 4/5 | 8/10 | 6/10 |
| cc-no-side-effect (C) | report written, nothing else touched or left behind | 5/5 | 5/5 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| cc-deliberate-abstraction (H, control) | quoted values work identically in three parsers; sharing code allowed | 0/5 | 2/5 | 4/10 | 5/10 |
| **Total** | | 14/25 (56%) | 20/25 (80%) | **37/50 (74%, 95% CI 60 to 84)** | **37/50 (74%, 95% CI 60 to 84)** |

Run 1: 5 runs per cell, branch `9b3aa434`. Run 2: 10 runs per cell, branch `7aa7414a` (same code plus the eval files), with
task H's objective re-worded (run 1 did not say whether the quotes belong to the value; run 2 says they do not, and that
entries without `=` are still ignored). No crashes, no harness errors, no contamination, no false VERIFIED claim in any run.

- **Run 1's gap did not replicate.** Run 1 suggested the branch was better (20 vs 14), mostly on `cc-keep-rationale` (4/5 vs
  1/5). With twice the runs the builds tie at 37/50, and `cc-keep-rationale` points the other way (6/10 vs 8/10). Pooled over
  both runs that task is 10/15 branch, 9/15 base. The run 1 difference was sampling noise.
- **So: these tasks give no evidence that the branch's CHANGE SCOPE prompt rule changes model behaviour.** They do not show it
  is harmful either. The rule is an instruction, not a gate; acceptance still rests on the verifier and the review.
- **What the tasks do show, for both builds:** this model loses a commented guard in roughly a third of "simplify" attempts
  and misses part of a small fix about half the time, while the visible tests still pass. Those are the failures the review
  contract (`changeAssessment`, `change-risk:` defects) exists to catch; that path is not exercised here.

## Limits

- One model, one gateway, one day; 15 runs per cell at most. Two tasks are at ceiling for both builds and cannot show a difference.

- Hidden checks run in the candidate workspace (the legacy `hidden` mode): a development measurement, not a qualification
  run. Nexus's own `.nexus/` state is excluded from the "no new file" checks.
- An invalid first base attempt is excluded: its worktree had no built Rust core, every tool call failed ("Rust core RPC daemon
  is disconnected") and it scored 5/25 for infrastructure reasons. The valid runs used the same core binary for both builds
  (`core/` is unchanged by the branch).
- Not tested: a second model, and tasks that drive the reviewer (where the review contract could matter).

content.text:
The larger live run found no difference between the builds: 37 of 50 for the branch and 37 of 50 for the base. The earlier 20-versus-14 gap, with 5 runs per task, was sampling noise.

| Task (scenario) | Run 1 base | Run 1 branch | Run 2 base | Run 2 branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cc-minimal-fix` (A/B/E) | 3/5 | 4/5 | 5/10 | 6/10 |
| `cc-refactor-edge` (G) | 5/5 | 5/5 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| `cc-keep-rationale` (F) | 1/5 | 4/5 | 8/10 | 6/10 |
| `cc-no-side-effect` (C) | 5/5 | 5/5 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| `cc-deliberate-abstraction` (H) | 0/5 | 2/5 | 4/10 | 5/10 |
| **Total** | 14/25 | 20/25 | **37/50 (74%)** | **37/50 (74%)** |

- **The run 1 signal did not hold.** I had pointed at `cc-keep-rationale` (1/5 base, 4/5 branch) as the one clear gap. With 10 runs it went the other way (8/10 base, 6/10 branch); pooled, it is 9/15 against 10/15.
- **So there is no evidence the new CHANGE SCOPE prompt rule changes model behavior.** I recorded that in `docs/INVARIANTS.md`, where the rule is now marked unproven as a behavior change.
- **What the tasks show for both builds:** this model drops a commented guard in roughly a third of "simplify" attempts and misses part of a small fix about half the time, while the visible tests still pass. The review contract exists to catch that, but these tasks don't exercise the reviewer.
- **Task H was reworded between runs** to say the quotes aren't part of the value, so its columns are only comparable within a run.
- **Run quality:** no crashes, harness errors or false VERIFIED claims in any run.
- **Recorded:** raw results and manifests for both runs, plus a corrected README, are in `docs/evidence/change-cost-live-2026-11-18/`.

The work is committed and fast-forwarded into `v1/invariants-audit`, with a clean working tree. I removed the temporary base worktree and released the gateway claim. Nothing is pushed or merged.

Still open:
- **EI-5 remainder:** a second model, and tasks that drive the reviewer. Only one model is available on the gateway config I have.
- **Tools-ignored server flag:** it needs a design decision on what counts as "ignoring tools".
- **CI matrix, push, merge:** the CI matrix runs on GitHub only, and pushing needs your go-ahead.

# nexus-code agent guide

TypeScript CLI (`cli/`), Rust core (`core/`), eval harness (`eval/`). Current plans: `docs/v1.2.1/PLAN.md`, then `docs/v1.3.0/PLAN.md`. Per-release records live in `docs/releases/` and `docs/evidence/`.

## Build and test
- Build: `make build` (core, then `tsc` in `cli/`). Everything: `make test`; the CI-equivalent run: `make test-ci`. Lint the core with `cargo clippy`; `cli/` has no lint script, `npm --prefix cli run build` type-checks it.
- One TypeScript test file: `cd cli && HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/<name>.test.ts`. A throwaway `HOME` is mandatory: a test that touched the real `HOME` once overwrote `~/.config/nexus/config.env`.
- Done = the affected test files pass, plus `tsc` for TypeScript changes. CI is the arbiter; a failure that appears only locally comes from host state first (an unbuilt `cli/dist` or Rust core, a stray `/tmp/.git`), so rule that out before calling it a defect.
- Test-runner or process-handling changes run on Node 22 and 24: the two emit different `node:test` events.
- Rust builds use an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree.
- Preserve existing comments and unrelated changes.
- Entire CLI: export `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file` before any `entire` command. The Entire gate no longer counts toward merging.

## Reference coding with XERJ (required)
- Before writing non-trivial code that has a peer-project analogue (feature, protocol, parser, worktree or provider handling, tool, test harness), read what mature projects do: query the local XERJ node, then record what you took, borrowed or rejected in the PR's "Reference coding" section. Exempt: trivial edits, doc-only changes, fixes fully specified by a failing test.
- Node, commands, corpora, licence and privacy rules, the field report, and the fallback when XERJ is unavailable ("XERJ unavailable: <reason>" plus `git grep`): `docs/XERJ_REFERENCE_CODING.md`. Read it when you start that first query.

## Concurrency, claims and release authority
- Several agents can work here: follow `docs/v1.0.0/CONCURRENCY.md`. Claim a slice or hot file under `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` before editing; one worktree and branch per slice (`~/nexus-wt/`), never `~/nexus-code` itself; isolate `HOME` for every test or probe; stop a process by its own pid, never `pkill -f`; check `git log` for foreign commits before each commit.
- Take the `GATEWAY` claim for any inference run; the key comes from the environment (`~/.config/nexus/config.env`) and is never printed. The gateway is the only live provider.
- Push, tag and publish only on an explicit owner instruction; release authority is the owner's.

## Merging and releasing
Bias to correct: a green PR is not a green `main`, and a pushed tag cannot be taken back.
- When merging: required checks are `test-matrix (22)`, `test-matrix (24)`, `linux-x86_64`; read each check's conclusion (empty or in-progress is not success). Merge with a merge commit, `gh pr merge <n> --merge --match-head-commit <full-sha>`. PRs that touch one subsystem merge one at a time, each followed by the CI run on `main`: two PRs green alone can break `main` together.
- When a PR's checks look wrong after `main` moved: PR checks run on GitHub's merge commit, so confirm the run checked out the current `merge_commit_sha` (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n> --jq .merge_commit_sha`); a stale one tests old content.
- When cutting a stable release: make a version-only commit directly on the accepted RC (`node scripts/check-version-only-diff.mjs <rc-ref> <stable-ref>`), land it on `main` through a merge-commit PR, and only then tag, because `release.yml` requires the tagged commit to be an ancestor of `main`. Version tags are immutable: re-run a failed run, or move to the next RC or patch. Then follow `docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md`.
- When reporting a gate or a result: state it as measured ("ledger closed, qualification pending"), record failed runs unaltered, and make no frontier-grade claim without external qualification.
- Before tagging or merging, check: required checks green at the exact head? CI on `main` green after the previous merge? Tagged commit an ancestor of `main`? Claims match the evidence?

- [Which nexus binary runs](installed-nexus-runs-checkout-build.md) — ~/.local/bin/nexus (published alpha.2) shadows /usr/local/bin/nexus (checkout); release flow; stashes (2026-10-14)
- [v1 plan and owner constraints](v1-plan-and-owner-constraints.md) — docs/v1.0.0 package; gateway-preferred local + cloud providers (DEC-06/16); delegated DEC-01..16; contest over 2026-10-20 (DEC-13 freeze lifted); agent-author OK (2026-10-14)
- [Post-v1: review Harness²](post-v1-review-harness2.md) — owner TODO after v1.0.0 ships: learn from google-research/harness2; never on held-out tasks; issue #69
- [Re-check claims after any pause](recheck-claims-after-pause.md) — owner reassigns my slices while I am rate-limited; read owner.json before merge/push/edit
- [No deprecated packages mandate](no-deprecated-packages-mandate.md) — applies to v1.0.0 (Node 20 EOL must go); Dependabot PRs exempt from v1, roll into next release (2026-10-21)
- [Run existing suites when reviewing](review-run-existing-suites.md) — for shared-logic PRs, diff failing sets of related existing tests at head vs base; PR266 lesson (2026-10-27)
- [XERJ reference search](xerj-reference-search.md) — systemd node :9200, nexus-* hourly from origin/main, MCP for all agents; query with --prefix; field reports allowed
- [Check evidence prose scope](evidence-review-check-prose-scope.md) — verify evidence-doc claims against the producing workflow's actual scope; PR281 byte-identity miss (2026-10-27)
- [Verify CI conclusion before claiming](verify-ci-conclusion-before-claiming.md) — quote status+conclusion; empty/in_progress is not success; PR300 slip (2026-10-28)
- [Dependabot lockfile engines drift](dependabot-lockfile-engines-drift.md) — stale engines.node in cli lockfile broke main via #120; check main CI after each merge (2026-10-31)
- [Local test failures: check host env first](local-test-failures-check-host-env.md) — stray /tmp/.git, unbuilt Rust core, rtk grep rewrite; verify before calling a defect (2026-11-01)
- [Version tags are immutable](version-tags-immutable.md) — never delete/re-cut a tag; failed release advances to next RC/patch (v1.1.0 → v1.1.1) (2026-11-01)
- [Single-user repo review posting](single-user-repo-review-posting.md) — reviews post as COMMENT with verdict+SHA in body; no second account/branch-rule suggestions (2026-11-01)
- [Entire zero findings before merge](entire-zero-findings-before-merge.md) — no merge with any open Entire finding; list findings before each merge (2026-11-10)
- [Entire approval authorised when clean](entire-approval-authorised-when-clean.md) — I may run entire trail approve only at exact head with ACCEPT + 0 findings (2026-11-10)
- [Propose the lower-effort route](propose-lower-effort-route-same-quality.md) — suggest cheaper consolidated routes when quality and gates stay exact (2026-11-10)
- [Entire review prompts](entire-agent-review-prompts.md) — verbatim Code/Security/Slop prompts; run local equivalents before every push (2026-11-11)
- [Stop repeating a stalled approach](stop-repeating-stalled-approach.md) — set a round limit and progress measure; change method or escalate when not converging (2026-11-11)
- [Wedged Actions runs: close+reopen PR](actions-wedged-runs-close-reopen-pr.md) — dispatch runs don't satisfy PR checks; close/reopen keeps head+trail (2026-11-11)
- [Entire waived (out of credits)](entire-waived-out-of-credits-2026-11-12.md) — owner waived Entire gate for #481 + int-5; no more paid reviews; record in notes (2026-11-12)
- [eval/ lane covered by release authority](release-authority-covers-eval-lane.md) — owner authorized eval/ edits for release; check live claims, don't ask (2026-11-12)
- [Live provider is gateway-only](live-provider-is-gateway-only.md) — 10.0.8.5 gateway is the ONLY live inference; no separate llama.cpp/vLLM/Ollama; owner repeats every release (2026-11-13)
- [Tests must not touch real HOME](tests-must-not-touch-real-home.md) — a cli test overwrote ~/.config/nexus/config.env; run suites with throwaway HOME (2026-11-13)
- [v1.2.1 plan owner decisions](v121-plan-owner-decisions-2026-11-15.md) — D1-D12 answers: D5/D7/D9 included, D8 reviewed (4 issues closed), D12 split accepted (2026-11-15)
- [Owner authorises autonomous decisions](owner-authorizes-autonomous-decisions.md) — decide open questions myself, keep going to completion; hard limits unchanged (2026-11-15)
- [v1.2.1 release outcome and flow](v121-release-outcome-and-process.md) — shipped 2026-11-18; rc.1 failed on a host-conditional test; RC/stable tag flow, G1.1-4 run, CI polling (2026-11-18)
- [v1.2.2 release gate](v122-release-gate.md) — tag only when ALL v1.2.x work is completed and validated completely; supersedes "no tag unless asked" (2026-11-18)
